K-017626.check: npx playwright test prints '3 passed' with no failures, and the column counts match 1, 2 and 4 at the three widths.
traps: Using minmax(300px, 1fr) causes horizontal overflow below 300px; use minmax(min(16rem, 100%), 1fr) instead.
Forgetting key on mapped Card elements gives React duplicate-key warnings and wrong reorders.
Putting media queries inside each card lets every card guess the layout instead of the grid deciding it.

steps.do: Mark the card wrapper as a size container in Card.module.css by setting container-type to inline-size.
Add an @container rule at min-width 24rem that changes .card from a column to a row with display flex.
Apply the wrapper class styles.wrapper in Card.jsx and keep the markup identical at every size.
Confirm the CSS file has exactly one @container rule.
Lint the component for unused imports after the change.
Render the card in a 280px container and a 640px container on the test page and check the flex direction in each.

K-017627.example: A .wrapper with container-type inline-size holds the card, and at 24rem and above .card switches to flex-direction row. The 280px sidebar keeps the column layout while the 640px main area shows the row layout.
K-017627.check: grep -c prints 1, and the Playwright test reports flex-direction row at 640px and column at 280px.
traps: Setting container-type on the same element that the @container rule styles does nothing; the query must target a container ancestor.
Using @media instead of @container makes the card react to the window width rather than its real space.
Using container-type size instead of inline-size can collapse the card height to zero.

steps.do: Create the image component file for the card.
Render an img with srcSet listing 480w, 960w and 1440w files and sizes set to (max-width: 600px) 100vw, 33vw.
Set width and height attributes to the intrinsic image size and style aspect-ratio as 16 / 9 with width 100%.
Set loading to lazy on every card image below the first visible row.
Count the files in the card folder that use srcSet.
Measure the card page with Lighthouse for layout shift.

K-017628.example: At a 700px viewport, sizes 33vw resolves to 231px, so a 2x screen loads the 480w file. A 16:9 box 400px wide reserves 225px of height before the image arrives.
K-017628.check: grep -rc srcSet prints 1 or more for CardImage.jsx, and the Lighthouse JSON reports cumulative-layout-shift numericValue below 0.1.
traps: Omitting width and height lets the card jump when the image arrives.
Using a plain src with no srcSet sends the largest file to phones.
Setting sizes to 100vw on a three-column grid downloads images about three times larger than needed.

steps.do: Create the hook file that exports useMediaQuery.
Write useMediaQuery with useState initialized from window.matchMedia(query).matches and a useEffect that adds a change listener and removes it in cleanup.
Call useMediaQuery('(max-width: 599px)') in Card.jsx and render the compact variant when it returns true.
Confirm no card code reads window.innerWidth directly.
Lint the hook file.
Run the card test that resizes the viewport to 375px and 800px and counts the action buttons at each size.

K-017629.example: useMediaQuery('(max-width: 599px)') returns true at 375px, so the card renders the compact variant with one action button. At 800px it returns false and the full variant with three action buttons renders.
K-017629.check: grep -rn innerWidth prints no lines, and the Playwright test reports 1 action button at 375px and 3 at 800px.
traps: Calling window.matchMedia during server render crashes; guard with typeof window !== 'undefined' or use a lazy useState initializer.
Forgetting to remove the change listener in the useEffect cleanup leaks handlers on unmount.
Reading window.innerWidth once in state does not update on resize unless a resize listener is added.

steps.do: Create the stylesheet for card actions.
Set min-height and min-width to 44px on .action with padding of 0.75rem 1rem.
Place the buttons in a flex row with flex-wrap set to wrap and a gap of 0.5rem.
List every button in the card folder to confirm each one uses the action class.
Run an axe accessibility scan on the cards page.
Run the test that measures each button bounding box at 375px.

K-017630.example: Each .action button at 375px measures 44px high and at least 96px wide, with an 8px gap between buttons on a 16px root font. The test asserts boundingBox().height >= 44 for every button in the card.
K-017630.check: npx playwright test prints '1 passed', and every button height in the test output is 44 or more.
traps: Setting only font-size leaves a 28px button, which is below the 44px target used here.
Setting min-height on the button text span instead of the button itself does not change the tap area.
Measuring at a desktop width hides the small-screen button size, so always measure at 375px.

steps.do: Set .title font-size to clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem) in Card.module.css.
Limit the title to 2 lines using display -webkit-box, -webkit-line-clamp 2 and overflow hidden.
Render the title as an h3 element with className styles.title in Card.jsx.
Confirm the clamp value is in the stylesheet.
Check the stylesheet formatting with prettier.
Render a 120-character title at 320px and count the visible lines in the browser test.

K-017631.example: At 320px the title font computes to 1rem, and at 1280px it reaches the 1.25rem maximum. A 120-character title shows exactly 2 lines followed by an ellipsis.
K-017631.check: grep -n clamp prints one line containing clamp(1rem, and the Playwright test reports 2 visible lines at 320px.
traps: Using px in clamp for the minimum and maximum ignores the user's browser font size setting; use rem.
Setting -webkit-line-clamp without display -webkit-box does nothing.
Omitting overflow hidden lets the hidden lines still push the card taller.

steps.do: Find the stylesheet files so you know which file holds the layout rules.
Count the existing media query rules to know the current breakpoint count.
Shrink the browser until the main column text wraps badly, and note that width in pixels, for example 600px.
Create the plan file, then write the breakpoint list into it by hand, with at most three breakpoints.

K-017632.example: The article text breaks into ragged lines below 600px, so the plan sets one breakpoint at 600px and a second at 960px where two columns fit. The plan keeps the total at three breakpoints or fewer.
K-017632.check: grep -c '@media' styles.css prints a number from 0 to 3, and ls layout-plan.md prints layout-plan.md.
traps: Choosing breakpoints for specific phone models, which go stale quickly. Plan breakpoints where the content breaks instead.

steps.do: Find all max-width media queries in the stylesheet.
Count min-width media queries, which are the mobile-first form.
If max-width queries outnumber min-width ones, plan to rewrite the base styles for the smallest screen first.
Set the plan rule that the base rules apply at 320px wide with no media query.

K-017633.example: grep finds 9 max-width rules and 2 min-width rules, so the plan converts the page to mobile-first with a 320px base and min-width steps at 640px and 1024px.
K-017633.check: After the plan is applied, grep -c 'min-width' styles.css reports at least as many rules as the chosen breakpoints, here 2.
traps: Mixing max-width and min-width in one file makes the cascade hard to reason about. The base layout must also work without any media query at all.

steps.do: List the current font-size declarations to see the fixed values in use.
Set the minimum body text size at 1rem so text stays readable on phones.
Set the maximum body text size at 1.25rem so text does not grow too large on wide screens.
Write the clamp value into the plan using the form clamp(min, preferred, max), with the preferred part mixing rem and vw.
Confirm the plan file contains a clamp value that starts at 1rem.

K-017634.example: The body text uses font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem), which gives 1rem at small widths and caps at 1.25rem on wide screens. The plan file records that value.
K-017634.check: grep -n 'clamp' layout-plan.md prints one line containing clamp(1rem, and 1.25rem.
traps: Using vw alone with no rem ignores the user's browser text size setting. Setting the minimum below 1rem fails accessibility for small text.

steps.do: Find existing card selectors so you know which elements to convert.
Check whether any container query rule already exists in the stylesheet.
Plan to set container-type to inline-size on the parent wrapper of the card.
Plan a named @container rule with min-width 480px that switches the card to a horizontal layout.

K-017635.example: The card-list wrapper gets container-type: inline-size and container-name: cards. The .card selector switches to display: grid with two columns inside @container cards (min-width: 480px).
K-017635.check: grep -c '@container' styles.css returns 0 before the change, and the plan lists one container name and one @container rule.
traps: Setting container-type on the card itself can collapse its inline size to zero. Using @media for a component that must respond to its parent ignores where the component is placed.

steps.do: Check whether the HTML page already declares a viewport meta tag.
Count the buttons that need to be tapped so the plan knows which controls to size.
Plan the meta tag exactly as width=device-width, initial-scale=1 in the head of index.html.
Plan a minimum target size of 44px by 44px for every button and nav link.
Confirm the head contains the meta tag with width=device-width.

K-017636.example: index.html has no viewport tag and 6 buttons. The plan adds a meta tag with width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and sets min-height and min-width of 44px on each button.
K-017636.check: grep -n 'width=device-width' index.html prints a line containing width=device-width, initial-scale=1 in the head.
traps: Adding user-scalable=no to the viewport tag blocks zoom and fails accessibility. Sizing touch targets with padding only can leave the hit area under 44px.

steps.do: Create the styles folder for global token files.
Create the empty token file src/styles/tokens.css.

Inside a :root block, declare --font-size-base as 1rem, --font-size-sm as 0.875rem, --font-size-lg as 1.25rem, --line-height-body as 1.5, and --space-1 as 0.25rem, --space-2 as 0.5rem, --space-4 as 1rem, --space-6 as 1.5rem.
Import tokens.css once at the top of src/main.tsx so every component can read the variables.
Count the space tokens to confirm all four are declared.

K-017637.example: The file declares --font-size-base: 1rem and --space-4: 1rem, so a 16px root gives 16px text and 16px spacing. A component then uses var(--space-4) and never a literal 16px.
K-017637.check: grep -c space- prints 4 and grep -c font-size- prints 3, matching the declared list.
traps: Declaring px for font sizes breaks user zoom settings.
Importing tokens.css inside a leaf component can load it late and cause a flash of unstyled text.
Writing the names without the leading -- means the browser ignores them.

steps.do: Create the components folder if it does not exist.
Create the file src/components/Text.tsx.
In Text.tsx, export type TextVariant as the union body, caption and heading, and map each variant to a class name such as text-body, text-caption and text-heading.
Define text-body with font-size var(--font-size-base) and line-height var(--line-height-body), and define text-caption with font-size var(--font-size-sm).
Type-check the project so the variant union rejects unknown values.

K-017638.example: <Text variant='caption'>Saved 2 min ago</Text> renders a span with class text-caption and font-size 0.875rem. Passing variant='large' fails tsc with a type error on the prop.
K-017638.check: npx tsc --noEmit exits with status 0 and no output for the valid usages; the deliberate variant='large' line produces error TS2322.
traps: Using a plain string type for variant lets typos compile silently.
Hard-coding 14px in the caption class ignores the token.
Forgetting to import the CSS file that defines text-body leaves the class with no styles.

steps.do: Add --container-max as 1120px and --container-pad as 1rem to the :root block in src/styles/tokens.css.
Create src/components/Container.tsx that renders a div with class container.
Add a rule .container with max-width var(--container-max), margin-inline auto, and padding-inline var(--container-pad).
Create a Playwright test file that sets the viewport to 1440 by 900 and asserts the container boundingBox width is 1120.
Run that one test file.

K-017639.example: At a 1440px viewport the container is 1120px wide and centered; at 375px it shrinks to 343px because the padding is 16px on each side. The Playwright test checks the 1440px case only.
K-017639.check: The Playwright run prints '1 passed' and the measured container width equals 1120px.
traps: Setting width instead of max-width stops the container shrinking on phones.
Forgetting padding-inline makes content touch the screen edge at 375px.
Testing at only one viewport misses the shrink case.

steps.do: Create the theme folder for the context file.
Create the file src/theme/ThemeContext.tsx.
In the file, export const tokens with fontSizeBase 16, lineHeightBody 1.5 and spaceUnit 4, then export const ThemeContext created with createContext and typed to that object.
Export function ThemeProvider using ThemeContext.Provider, and export function useTokens that calls useContext and throws if the value is undefined.
Count the export lines to confirm the four exports exist.
Type-check the project.

K-017640.example: Wrapping <App /> in <ThemeProvider> lets any child call useTokens().spaceUnit and get 4. Calling useTokens outside a provider throws an error that names the missing provider.
K-017640.check: grep -c export prints 4 and tsc exits with status 0.
traps: Calling useContext with no provider returns undefined, so the throw guard is required.
Copying token values into both CSS and JavaScript lets them drift apart.
Creating the token object inside the component body makes a new object on every render.

steps.do: Add --grid-gutter as 1rem to the :root block in src/styles/tokens.css.
Create src/components/Grid.tsx that exports Grid, taking columns typed as 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 and children.
Set the style prop to display grid, gridTemplateColumns to repeat(columns, minmax(0, 1fr)), and gap to var(--grid-gutter).
Add a media query in src/styles/grid.css that sets .grid to one column below 640px, and import grid.css from src/main.tsx.
Lint the component file.
Confirm the minmax rule is present in the component.

K-017641.example: <Grid columns={3}> at 1024px renders three equal columns with a 16px gap. At 500px the media query forces one column.
K-017641.check: npx eslint exits with status 0 and no errors, and grep -c minmax prints 1.
traps: Using repeat(columns, 1fr) instead of minmax(0, 1fr) lets long content push columns wider.
Setting gap in px instead of var(--grid-gutter) breaks the token.
Forgetting to import grid.css leaves the single-column rule unapplied.

steps.do: Create an empty file at src/components/Stack.tsx.
Export a Stack function that takes children, direction as 'column' or 'row', and gap typed as the union 1 | 2 | 4 | 6.
Set the style prop to display flex, flex-direction from direction, and gap to var(--space-N) where N is the gap value.
Format the file with Prettier to confirm consistent style.
Type-check the project.

K-017642.example: <Stack direction='row' gap={4}> sets style gap to var(--space-4), which is 1rem. A gap of 3 is not in the union, so tsc reports an error.
K-017642.check: Prettier prints 'All matched files use Prettier code style!' and tsc exits with status 0.
traps: Typing gap as number accepts values with no token behind them.
Setting gap in px instead of var(--space-N) breaks the scale.
Forgetting display flex makes gap do nothing.

steps.do: Create the project folder.
Create the page file inside it.
In menu.html, add a button with id menu-toggle, aria-expanded=false, and aria-controls=menu-list, then add a ul with id menu-list and the hidden attribute.
Count aria-expanded attributes to confirm the trigger has exactly one.
Run axe on the served page to check button name and ARIA errors.

K-017643.example: A button with aria-expanded="false" opens ul#menu-list, which starts with the hidden attribute. A click handler in menu.js sets both aria-expanded to true and removes hidden.
K-017643.check: grep prints 1 and axe reports 0 violations for button-name and aria-allowed-attr.
traps: Do not use a div as the toggle, because it gets no keyboard focus or button role. Do not change hidden without also changing aria-expanded, or screen readers announce the wrong state.

steps.do: Create the script file beside menu.html.
In menu.js, add a keydown listener on the element with role=menu that moves focus with ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End, wrapping at both ends.
Set tabindex=-1 on every role=menuitem except the first, and call focus() on the item that becomes active.
Count role=menuitem attributes in menu.html so you can match the expected item total.
Run the Playwright test that presses ArrowDown on the last item and checks that focus wraps to the first item.

K-017644.example: With 4 items, pressing ArrowDown on item 4 sets focus to item 1 using the index (i+1)%4. The test asserts document.activeElement.textContent equals the first item label.
K-017644.check: grep prints 4 and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Do not put tabindex=0 on every item, because that puts all of them in the tab order. Do not attach the arrow listener to the button alone; it belongs on the role=menu element.

steps.do: Open menu.js so you can add the close logic.
Add a keydown check for the key value Escape that sets hidden on menu-list, sets aria-expanded to false, and calls focus() on menu-toggle.
Check that the Escape handler exists in the script.
Run the Playwright test that opens the menu, presses Escape, and checks that document.activeElement is menu-toggle.

K-017645.example: A user opens the menu from the button, then presses Escape. The handler hides ul#menu-list, sets aria-expanded to false, and focuses button#menu-toggle within the same keydown event.
K-017645.check: grep prints one line number and Playwright reports 1 passed with active element id menu-toggle.
traps: Do not close on any key other than Escape, because Tab should still move focus out normally. Do not forget to restore focus; a hidden list that leaves focus on removed elements loses the user's place.

steps.do: Create the stylesheet beside menu.html.
Add a rule .menu a:focus-visible with outline 3px solid and outline-offset 2px, and add min-width 44px and min-height 44px to .menu a.
Confirm the focus-visible rule is present.
Confirm the 44px size value appears in the stylesheet.
Run the Lighthouse accessibility audit on the menu page.

K-017646.example: Link text #767676 on a #ffffff background measures 4.54:1, which passes AA for 16px text. The focus outline uses a 3px solid ring, and each link is at least 44px tall.
K-017646.check: grep prints one line for focus-visible and one for 44px, and Lighthouse reports an accessibility score of 100.
traps: Do not remove the focus outline with outline:none and rely on color alone. Do not use 44px only on the text span, because the clickable area is the a element.

steps.do: Create the page file for the disclosure menu.
In index.html, wrap a ul of links in a details element and give the summary element the text Menu.
Count details elements to confirm there is exactly one menu.
Run axe on the page to check that the summary element has an accessible name.

K-017647.example: A summary with the text Menu toggles the nested ul of three links. The browser handles Enter and Space on the summary without any script.
K-017647.check: grep prints 2 (open and close tags on one line count as separate matches) and axe reports 0 violations for summary-name.
traps: Do not add role=button to summary, because it already has the correct role. Do not add role=menu to the link list, because plain navigation links should not use the menu pattern.

steps.do: Open menu.html to edit the nav element.
Add aria-label=Main to the nav element and aria-current=page to the link for the active page.
Count aria-current attributes to confirm exactly one link is marked.
Run axe to check for landmark and label errors.
Run the Playwright test that tabs through the nav and checks the link with aria-current.

K-017648.example: The Home link carries aria-current=page, so screen readers announce it as the current page. The nav element has aria-label Main, which separates it from a footer nav.
K-017648.check: grep prints 1, axe reports 0 landmark violations, and Playwright reports 1 passed.
traps: Do not put aria-current on every link or on a parent li only. Do not leave the nav unlabeled when there is more than one nav on the page.

steps.do: List foreground color usages in menu files.
Set body text contrast to at least 4.5:1 against the menu background.
Set large text and icons to at least 3:1 contrast.
Locate the asset catalog where the adaptive named colors will go.

K-017649.example: MenuTokens.labelPrimary is a named color with a light value of 0.11 gray on a 0.98 white background, a ratio of about 16:1. The find command returns ./App/Assets.xcassets, where the new colorset will be added.
K-017649.check: Each planned text color pair reports a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for both light and dark variants, and find prints at least one Assets.xcassets path.
traps: Small models often use system gray for disabled text without computing its contrast ratio.
Do not hardcode Color(red:green:blue:) values that ignore dark mode.
Contrast must be checked for both light and dark variants, not only the light one.

steps.do: Run the parity test that compares the key sets of all ARB files.
Count the top-level entries in the English ARB file, including the @@locale entry.
Count the top-level entries in the German ARB file the same way.
Check that the German ARB file is valid JSON.

K-017650.example: app_en.arb and app_de.arb both report 15 entries, and the parity test prints All 14 translation keys match because @@locale is excluded. If the German file lacks onboardingSkip, the test fails and names that key.
K-017650.check: flutter test ends with All tests passed!, and both jq counts print the same number.
traps: Comparing only the key count misses a renamed key when the total still matches.
Keys that start with @ are metadata, so exclude them from the translation count.
A JSON syntax error stops jq with a parse error before any key is compared.

steps.do: Regenerate the localization code from the ARB files.
Count the translation keys in the template ARB file, excluding entries that start with @.
Count the abstract declarations in the generated class, which covers both getters and methods with placeholders.
Confirm the generated file passes the Dart analyzer.

K-017651.example: The template has 12 messages, and grep reports 12 declarations in lib/l10n/app_localizations.dart. The file is generated there because l10n.yaml sets output-dir to lib/l10n and synthetic-package to false.
K-017651.check: The two counts match, and dart analyze prints No issues found!
traps: Counting only String get misses messages with placeholders, which generate methods instead.
The localeName field is not a message, so it must not be counted.
Changing the generated file by hand is lost on the next gen-l10n run.

steps.do: Run the onboarding golden test without updating images to see current diffs.
Regenerate the golden PNGs only after you have reviewed the intended change.
List the PNG files created for every locale and page.
Run the whole onboarding test folder once more to confirm it passes against the new images.

K-017652.example: The test loops over en, de and ar for three pages and calls matchesGoldenFile with names such as goldens/welcome_ar.png, creating 9 PNG files. After pumpAndSettle, a rerun with no changes prints All tests passed!.
K-017652.check: find prints 9 file paths, and flutter test ends with All tests passed! with no golden mismatch messages.

Skipping pumpAndSettle leaves animations mid-frame, so the image changes between runs.
A locale missing from the loop lowers coverage without any error.

steps.do: Open the RTL widget test that pumps the onboarding flow with the ar locale and Directionality set to TextDirection.rtl.
Run the RTL layout test file.
Search onboarding code for hardcoded left-side padding that does not mirror.
Run the analyzer on the onboarding code.

K-017653.example: In the test, the Next button's tester.getSize height is 48.0, which satisfies greaterThanOrEqualTo(44.0). The grep prints no lines because padding uses EdgeInsetsDirectional.
K-017653.check: flutter test ends with All tests passed!, grep prints nothing, and dart analyze prints No issues found!
traps: EdgeInsets.only(left:) does not mirror in RTL, so use EdgeInsetsDirectional.
Testing only the English locale never exercises the RTL path.
Measuring a Text widget instead of the tappable button checks the wrong size.

steps.do: Run the plural test that checks counts 0, 1, 2 and 5 in each locale.
Confirm the ARB message uses the plural keyword and a count placeholder.
Regenerate the localizations so the plural method exists in the generated class.
Check that the generated plural method takes an int count parameter.

K-017654.example: The stepsLeft message with count 1 renders 1 step left in en, and count 5 renders 5 steps left. The test asserts exact strings for 4 counts across 2 locales, which is 8 expectations.
K-017654.check: flutter test prints All tests passed!, and grep prints the int count parameter line in the plural method.
traps: Russian and Arabic have more plural categories than one and other, so an ARB with only those two fails for them.
Adding an s suffix in code ignores each locale's rules.
A count placeholder not typed as int breaks plural selection.

steps.do: Search onboarding code for Text widgets with single-quoted literals.
Search onboarding code for Text widgets with double-quoted literals.
Run the locale switch timing test.
Confirm the timing test pumps for exactly 200 milliseconds after the language change.

K-017655.example: Both greps print no lines for lib/onboarding. The switch test taps the German chip, pumps Duration(milliseconds: 200), and finds the text Willkommen.
K-017655.check: Both greps print nothing, flutter test ends with All tests passed!, and the last grep prints one line that contains milliseconds: 200.

Interpolated strings built with dollar signs can hide literal text, so read the matches.
Strings in widget files outside lib/onboarding are not covered by this search.

steps.do: Read the current design tokens file if one exists.
Write a table with four roles: item title uses body, shortcut uses callout, section header uses footnote, and hint uses caption.
Decide that no menu role may call Font.system(size:) directly.
Measure the count of direct size calls in menu files. The count must be exactly 0.

K-017656.example: MenuTokens maps itemTitle to .body, shortcutHint to .callout, and sectionHeader to .footnote. The rg count prints nothing, which means 0 matches under Sources/Menu, so no custom size is needed.
K-017656.check: The role table has exactly four rows, and the rg count for Sources/Menu is 0 (no output lines).

Do not map shortcut hints to .caption2 because that is too small for many users to read.
If cat reports the file is missing, say so and do not invent its contents.

steps.do: Install the Playwright test runner as a dev dependency.
Download the Chromium build that Playwright drives.
Create tests/form-validation.spec.js that fills the email field with bad-address and reads input.validity.typeMismatch.
Run only that spec file.
Confirm the summary reports zero failures.

K-017657.example: The test fills #email with bad-address and expects typeMismatch to be true and form.checkValidity() to return false. A second test leaves #name empty and expects valueMissing to be true.
K-017657.check: The runner prints a line like '2 passed' and no line containing 'failed'.

A form with the novalidate attribute skips all native checks, so remove it before testing.

steps.do: Install html-validate as a dev dependency.
Run the linter on the form page.
Confirm the linter printed no error lines and exited with code 0.
Temporarily change one input to type=emial and run the linter again.
Confirm the linter names the type attribute in one error line and exits with code 1.

Restoring the typo file to type=email before running the final check is easy to forget.
Linting a different file than the one that was edited gives a false pass.

steps.do: Install Playwright as a dev dependency if it is not already present.
Create tests/tap-target.spec.js that loops over input, button, and select elements and reads each boundingBox.
Set the viewport to 390 pixels wide and 844 pixels tall, then assert each box height and width is at least 44 pixels.
Run the tap target spec.
Confirm the failure list is empty.

K-017659.example: At a 390 by 844 viewport, #submit must have a boundingBox height of at least 44. A checkbox with a 16px box fails and needs a larger label hit area.
K-017659.check: The runner prints passed with 0 failed and no assertion error that mentions expected 44.

Treating 1rem as 44px without checking the root font size gives the wrong size.
Running at a desktop viewport means the mobile rules never apply.
